Check governing headings, definitions, exceptions and current source.","text":"Temporary absences up to 52 weeks
78254 A person should be treated as living in their home for any period of temporary absence of not

more than 52 weeks if1


1. they intend to return to live in the home2 and


2. the part of the home they normally live in has not been let or sub-let to another person 3 and


3. they


      3.1 are detained in custody on remand pending trial or


      3.2 are detained pending sentence upon conviction or


      3.3 are required to live as a condition of bail in either


            3.3.a a dwelling other than a dwelling he occupies as his home or


            3.3.b an approved bail hostel or


            3.3.c an approved probation hostel4 or


      3.4 are resident in a hospital or similar institution as a patient 5 or


      3.5 are, or their partner, or a person under the age of 20 for whom the claimant or partner is
      responsible, is undergoing


            3.5.a medical treatment or


            3.5.b medically approved convalescence


      in the UK or elsewhere, in accommodation that is not a care home 6 or


      3.6 are on a training course in the UK or elsewhere 7 or


      3.7 are providing medically approved care for another person who is living in the UK or elsewhere 8
      or


      3.8 are caring for a person under the age of 20 whose parent or guardian is temporarily absent

      from their home because they are receiving medically approved care or treatment 9 or


      3.9 are


             3.9.a living in the UK or elsewhere and


             3.9.b receiving medically approved care


      in accommodation that is not a care home10 or independent hospital or


      3.10 are a F/T student to whom DMG 78225 and 78231 2. do not apply11 or


      3.11 are receiving care in a care home or independent hospital, other than as in DMG 78240 12 or


      3.12 have left the home because of fear of violence


             3.12.a in that home or


             3.12.b by a former partner or


             3.12.c by a close relative


             and DMG 78231 1. does not apply13 and


4. the absence is unlikely to


      4.1 exceed 52 weeks or


      4.2 substantially exceed 52 weeks in exceptional circumstances 14 (for example where a claimant
      has gone into hospital or has to live in a hostel as a condition of bail).


    1 SPC Regs, Sch II, para 4(11) & (12); 2 Sch II, para 4(11)(a); 3 Sch II, para 4(11)(b); 4 Sch II, para 4(11)(c)(i);

Concept role: dwp:Applicability.","text":"Source-bounded navigation through DMG 78065–78076, separate from ignoring a person’s presence under 78077–78080 and from deciding whether partners remain one household. Normal residence is where a person usually lives: exceptional visits or absences are disregarded, and temporary absence does not itself change the normal home. DMG 78067 requires factual consideration of time, frequency, permanence, intentions, circumstances, degree of sharing, services, other accommodation and liabilities. An address, university term or overnight stay alone does not settle that assessment. Sharing only a bathroom, lavatory or communal area, or separate legal payment liabilities to the same landlord, has the captured sharing exceptions. Kitchen sharing can exist without entering or using it when personal items are stored or meals prepared there; merely passing through to a self-contained flat is different. DMG 78072–78075 require the contractual capacity and intention to create legal relations, an obligation for occupation from a recognised source of law, and the stipulated connection between non-payment and ending the licence or lease; another liability to a third party is not the same-landlord condition. Retain the England-and-Wales scope and presumption in the captured capacity passage rather than infer incapacity from a diagnosis. For an overnight carer, establish the separate address, actual use and frequency, postal address and Council Tax registration. All residence and contractual facts remain unknown until evidenced. A finding about this residence condition is not a finding of benefit entitlement, ignored-person status or continuing couple membership."}},{"paths":[{"assertions":["https://chris-page-gov.github.io/okf-dwp/id/assertion/location-migration/d24603e1125a97beb241758ab1481ce48f661c75fa8c5d20b79ddfd35ee52721","https://chris-page-gov.github.io/okf-dwp/id/assertion/source-reference/ac91ff8577fb0245b085920b50256fb3d20e24d2fc74f7a2ae0d4e91efbce338","https://chris-page-gov.github.io/okf-dwp/id/assertion/source-reference/4ed502a6021a23f545f198dd6b5bd91152171510252e05ee934746b15ae7a73a"],"records":["https://chris-page-gov.github.io/okf-dwp/id/staff-domain/partner","https://chris-page-gov.github.io/okf-dwp/id/unit/dmg/dmg-vol13-ch77/manual-structure-v1/source-0000032784-000-8b46ddc0e915","https://chris-page-gov.github.io/okf-dwp/id/unit/dmg/dmg-vol13-ch77/manual-structure-v1/source-0000013997-000-2a724f8ec070","https://chris-page-gov.github.io/okf-dwp/id/unit/dmg/dmg-vol13-ch77/manual-structure-v1/source-0000007057-000-2d15bc718c74"],"seed":"https://chris-page-gov.github.io/okf-dwp/id/staff-domain/partner"}],"reasons":["Followed http://purl.org/dc/terms/references from https://chris-page-gov.github.io/okf-dwp/id/unit/dmg/dmg-vol13-ch77/manual-structure-v1/source-0000013997-000-2a724f8ec070"],"record":{"access":"public","assertion_status":"normalized","authority":{"class":"derived","label":"Exact frozen source spans; logical boundary proposal; applicability unreviewed","source":"https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/68401a731d85c6606009cce4/dmgch77.pdf"},"evidence_unit":{"boundary_status":"machine-detected","completeness":"unresolved","joiner":"

77016 A polygamous marriage case is one in which1


1. a person (the person in question) is a husband or wife by virtue of a marriage entered into in a country
which permits polygamy and


2. either party to the marriage has for the time being any spouse additional to the other party and


3. the


         3.1 person in question and


         3.2 other party to the marriage and


         3.3 additional spouse


         are members of the same household.


Note 1: The DM should obtain evidence of the marriage, if a claimant declares more than one spouse.


Note 2: See DMG 77140 et seq where one or more members of a polygamous marriage are mixed-age.


                                                                                        1 SPC Act 02, s 12(1)
